item.title: Gustave Africa's Most Wanted Predator Nobody Can Kill
item.description:
Gustave is a giant Nile crocodile from Burundi's Ruzizi River and Lake Tanganyika, estimated at 18-20 feet and around 2,000 lbs, and blamed for as many as 300 human deaths. How much of that is documented fact, and how much is legend?
In Part 1 of the Gustave Files, we separate the record from the myth: what naturalist Patrice Faye actually measured, why the death toll is disputed (later estimates put it closer to 60), the bullet scars he carries, and the 32-foot trap that stayed empty.
We also look at the biology of an exceptionally large male Nile crocodile: why size like this changes what a predator can hunt, and why he became the most feared crocodile in Africa.
Gustave is estimated to have hatched around 1955. His last rumored sighting was in 2015, and reports of his death have never been verified.
▶ Part 2 is coming next: the expeditions that came closest to catching him.
